version.changelog: 支持 v1.1.0（硅基流动）和 v1.2.0+（阿里云百炼）双版本；说明 mcporter 加载 ~/.cursor/mcp.json 和 ~/.claude.json；输出改为去口语化的精简原始文案

llm.summary: The skill mostly matches its Douyin video-analysis purpose, but its setup and troubleshooting instructions can expose API keys and read local MCP configuration too broadly.

dimensions.detail: Use of browser and mcporter is coherent for Douyin collection and transcription, but local config inspection and credential-bearing command examples are broader than necessary and can leak secrets into logs or transcripts.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Setup uses npm install -g mcporter and an unpinned uvx douyin-mcp-server path for the latest version, creating ordinary supply-chain risk for a local tool that receives API credentials.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill directs agents to inspect ~/.cursor/mcp.json and ~/.claude.json without an explicit consent boundary; the main skill prints only args and env key names, but troubleshooting prints the full config object.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No backdoor, scheduled task, memory write, or privilege escalation is present; the persistent elements are user MCP configuration and optional global CLI installation.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The main browser and douyin-mcp workflow is purpose-aligned, but troubleshooting prints the full douyin-mcp configuration, which can include plaintext API keys and is not needed for video analysis.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable with a skill that uses a browser profile, local MCP configuration, and API-backed transcription. Do not run the troubleshooting config-dump command with real credentials unless it is redacted first, avoid pasting API keys into shell commands or support chats, and prefer pinned, reviewed versions of mcporter and douyin-mcp-server.
llm.findings:
[SDI-2] expected: Checking which douyin-mcp key name is configured supports version selection, but reading user-local MCP config still needs clearer consent and minimization.
[SQP-2] unexpected: The lack of a warning or consent boundary for local MCP config inspection is supported by the artifact and remains a real concern.
[SQP-3] expected: The Chinese-only documentation is visible, but for a Douyin-focused workflow this is a usability/localization note rather than a security basis for escalation.
[T09] unexpected: The troubleshooting command serializes the full douyin-mcp configuration with json.dumps(cfg), which can print plaintext API credentials.
[T09] unexpected: Examples place API keys directly in shell command text; invoking a credentialed MCP tool is expected, but embedding literal keys in commands is unnecessary and increases log/history exposure.
[T08] expected: Installing mcporter and running douyin-mcp are expected for this skill, but unpinned package resolution is a supply-chain risk users should review.
